notable.grandline.clementine.title: Mayor of Orange Town, Keeper of the Old Orchard
dialogue.grandline.notable.clementine: Clementine Daidai, mayor. Mind the east rows — they're older than the town hall and better behaved.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.why: Three days before the Marmalade Festival, Rotgut's still-house pirates seized Orange Town's orchards to turn the whole harvest into cheap liquor. The town band scattered, and a festival without music is just a funeral with oranges.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.cast.carme: 'Brass Thunder', the town's bartender-trumpeter. Ate the Bell-Bell Fruit as a child and rings like a cathedral; her songs put tired bodies back in tune.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.cast.cleme: mayor of Orange Town and keeper of the old orchard. Small, fierce, and older than most of the trees.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.cast.rotgu: Wendell 'Rotgut' Mostaccio, distiller-pirate. Wants every orange in the East Blue in his still, and the last bottle priced like treasure.
arc.grandline.decision.orange_plan: between the festival and the fuses (talk to Carmen)
arc.grandline.site.orange_cannery: the old cannery in the hills, where the band's instruments are
arc.grandline.site.orange_fuses: the fuse lines under the orchard rows
quest.grandline.orange_band.desc: Carmen's band ran when Rotgut came, but their instruments didn't. Ask 2 townsfolk where the musicians are hiding, and take the instruments back from 3 of Rotgut's men at the old cannery.
quest.grandline.orange_still.desc: Carmen's little brother Pepe is chained to Rotgut's biggest still. Break 4 of the still-house guards and get him out.
quest.grandline.orange_choice.desc: Rotgut bottles his last batch tonight, then lights the fuses under the orchard. Carmen and Mayor Clementine disagree about what comes first. Talk to Carmen and decide.
quest.grandline.orange_festival.desc: Bring Mayor Clementine to the bandstand to open the Marmalade Festival — right under Rotgut's nose.
quest.grandline.orange_fuses.desc: Oil-soaked fuses run under the east orchard rows. Beat 3 of Rotgut's men guarding them before he can light them.
scene.grandline.orange_1.end.1: narrator|Orange Town smells of oranges and smoke. The festival lanterns hang unlit over boarded-up stalls.
scene.grandline.orange_1.end.2: carmen|You hear that? No? EXACTLY. No music in Orange Town since Rotgut came. Three days to the Marmalade Festival, and the band's scattered to the four winds.
scene.grandline.orange_1.end.3: carmen|I'm Carmen. Bartender, trumpeter, Bell-Bell Fruit — I can ring like a cathedral. But a one-woman band is just noise with ambition.
scene.grandline.orange_1.end.5: carmen|Rotgut's still-house pirates took the orchards and the old cannery. The boys ran; the instruments didn't. Ask around town — somebody knows where my musicians are hiding.
scene.grandline.orange_1.end.6: carmen|Find them, get their instruments back, and I'll play you something that'll put the colour back in your cheeks. That's not a figure of speech. That's what the fruit does.
scene.grandline.orange_band.end.1: narrator|At the old cannery the band's instruments lie in a heap: a tuba full of orange peel, a snare drum with a boot through it, three bent bugles.
scene.grandline.orange_band.end.2: carmen|My babies! Oh, the tuba. What did they DO to the tuba?
scene.grandline.orange_band.end.3: carmen|Everyone's back but Pepe, the big drum. The trombones say Rotgut's men took him up to the still-house to keep the fires going. Pepe can't say no to anyone. It's his worst quality and his best one.
scene.grandline.orange_band.end.4: carmen|The still-house is up past the orchard. Please. He's my little brother.
scene.grandline.orange_still.end.1: narrator|Pepe is chained to the biggest still, feeding the fire with orange-wood and crying a little. Around the still-house, oil-soaked fuses run out into the orchard rows like roots.
scene.grandline.orange_still.end.2: carmen|Pepe! Are you hurt? Did they feed you? Why are you crying?
scene.grandline.orange_still.end.3: pepe|The oranges, Carmen. He's bottling the last batch tonight, and then he lights the fuses. 'The last orange liquor in the East Blue,' he says. 'Priced accordingly.'
scene.grandline.orange_still.end.4: clementine|Seventy years I've kept that orchard. My grandmother planted the east rows. He'll burn them for a price tag?
scene.grandline.orange_still.end.5: carmen|Not if we make a lot of noise first.
scene.grandline.orange_choice.talk.1: carmen|Here's my plan. We play the festival TONIGHT, right in the square, right under his nose. Rotgut can't stand people being happy for free — he'll come down to stop it himself.
scene.grandline.orange_choice.talk.2: carmen|And while you fight him, the band plays. The Bell-Bell tone puts bodies back in tune. You'll feel it: every bruise and scratch, singing back into place.
scene.grandline.orange_choice.talk.3: clementine|And while you're dancing, his men light the fuses. Half the east orchard goes up. Seventy years.
scene.grandline.orange_choice.talk.4: clementine|My plan: cut the fuses first. All of them. Then deal with Rotgut. No festival this year — but there'll be an orchard for the next one.
scene.grandline.orange_choice.talk.5: carmen|A year without a festival, Mayor. Do you know what that does to a town?
scene.grandline.orange_choice.talk.6: clementine|Do you know what fire does to one? Decide, traveller. We'll both live with it.
scene.grandline.choice.orange_plan.festi: Play the festival tonight. Let Rotgut come to the music.
scene.grandline.choice.orange_plan.fuses: Cut the fuses first. Save the orchard, even if the festival waits a year.
scene.grandline.orange_choice.end.festiv: carmen|YES! Mayor, you have to open it — tradition. Band, places! One, two, three, FOUR!
clementine|Good. The fuses run under the east rows. Quietly, now — Rotgut's men are posted all along them.
scene.grandline.orange_festival.end.1: clementine|By the authority of the Old Orchard and the Town Council of Orange Town... the Marmalade Festival is OPEN!
scene.grandline.orange_festival.end.2: narrator|The band strikes up. Lanterns flare along the street. For one ridiculous minute the whole town dances — then the still-house doors bang open up the hill.
scene.grandline.orange_fuses.end.1: narrator|The last fuse comes up out of the dirt like a dead snake. The east rows stand dark and safe.
scene.grandline.orange_fuses.end.2: clementine|There. Let him come. He'll find nothing to burn.
scene.grandline.orange_2.start.1: rotgut|Oranges! Glorious oranges! Every one of them going into my still. You want to stop that? Come on, then.
rotgut|WHAT is that NOISE? Who said you could have a festival? I've got a schedule! I've got a LAUNCH!
scene.grandline.orange_2.start.fuses.1: rotgut|My fuses! Somebody pulled my fuses! Do you know how much LAMP OIL that was?
scene.grandline.orange_2.start.fuses.2: rotgut|Fine. FINE. I'll do it the old-fashioned way. Starting with you.
scene.grandline.orange_2.end.1: narrator|Rotgut goes down among his own barrels. The siege of Orange Town is over.
scene.grandline.orange_2.end.festival.1: narrator|Rotgut goes down in a spray of his own product. The crowd roars. The band never misses a beat.
scene.grandline.orange_2.end.festival.2: narrator|Up the hill, a fuse fizzes its last few yards. The east orchard goes up in a sheet of orange flame. The town forms a bucket line — still dancing.
scene.grandline.orange_2.end.festival.3: clementine|...Seventy years. Well. Trees grow back. Festivals don't, if you skip enough of them.
scene.grandline.orange_2.end.fuses.1: narrator|Rotgut goes down among his own barrels. The orchard stands dark and whole behind him.
scene.grandline.orange_2.end.fuses.2: clementine|Every row. Every single row. Orange Town owes you, traveller. The shops will know it by morning.
scene.grandline.orange_2.end.fuses.3: carmen|No festival this year... but I can hear next year's from here.
scene.grandline.recruit_carmen.start.1: narrator|Carmen is sitting on the edge of the bandstand, polishing a trumpet that is already gleaming.
scene.grandline.recruit_carmen.end.1: carmen|I want to play a song in every port in the world, and one at the end of it. A crew needs a band. Ask me, Captain.
scene.grandline.recruit_carmen.end.2: carmen|The fishermen say there's trouble at Syrup Village's regatta. Clockwork sharks. Honestly.
scene.grandline.recruit_carmen.end.festi: carmen|Did you SEE them? The whole town, dancing in the middle of a pirate fight! Best gig I've ever played.
carmen|I've played every bar in Orange Town. I want to play every port in the world — and one at the end of it, where the Saltfire burns.
carmen|A crew needs a band. Somebody to keep the beat, and to put you back together afterwards. That's me. One, two, three, four — ask me, Captain.
carmen|Oh — and the fishermen say there's a regatta at Syrup Village where a pirate's racing clockwork sharks. That sounds like it needs a soundtrack.
scene.grandline.recruit_carmen.end.fuses: carmen|No festival. You know what? Mayor Clementine was right. I hate it, but she was right.
carmen|Next year I'll play the biggest Marmalade Festival this town has ever seen — or I'll be out there somewhere, playing a port nobody's heard of yet.
carmen|A crew needs a band. Somebody to keep the beat, and to put you back together afterwards. That's me. Ask me, Captain — before I change my mind and stay for the trees.
carmen|The fishermen say there's a regatta at Syrup Village where a pirate's racing clockwork sharks. That sounds like it needs a soundtrack.
recap.grandline.orange_1: Reached Orange Town three days before the Marmalade Festival and met Carmen 'Brass Thunder', whose band had scattered.
recap.grandline.orange_band: Found the hidden musicians and took their instruments back from Rotgut's men at the old cannery.
recap.grandline.orange_still: Freed Carmen's brother Pepe from the still-house — and found the fuses Rotgut means to light under the orchard.
recap.grandline.orange_choice.festival: Decided to play the festival right under Rotgut's nose.
recap.grandline.orange_choice.fuses: Decided to cut the fuses before facing Rotgut.
recap.grandline.orange_festival: Mayor Clementine opened the Marmalade Festival, and the town danced.
recap.grandline.orange_fuses: Pulled every fuse out of the orchard rows.
recap.grandline.orange_2: Rotgut fell among his own barrels.
recap.grandline.orange_2.festival: Beat Rotgut in the middle of the festival while the band played on — but the east orchard burned.
recap.grandline.orange_2.fuses: Beat Rotgut with the orchard safe behind you. Orange Town owes you.
recap.grandline.recruit_carmen: Carmen wants to play every port in the world. She'll join if you ask — and there's trouble at Syrup Village's regatta.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.bonus.fest: Half of Orange Town saw you beat Rotgut while the band played. They'll tell the story for years — and the east orchard burned while they danced.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.bonus.fuse: The orchards are saved. Mayor Clementine presses a crate of provisions on you, and Orange Town's shops give you 15% off from now on.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.aid.festiv: Carmen's trumpet rings out across the square. The Bell-Bell tone runs through your bones, and your wounds close as the band plays.
arc.grandline.recruit_hint.carmen: Carmen will join your crew if you ask: talk to her and invite her aboard.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.after.carm: Still no band big enough for me in this town. ...That was a hint, Captain.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.during.cle: Mayor Clementine. If you've come for the festival, it's cancelled. If you've come to un-cancel it, I'm listening.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.after.clem: The orchard's quiet again. Quiet is good. Quiet means growing.
The east rows will take ten years. The festival took one night. I'm told that's the right way round. I'm not sure yet.
Every row standing. Come by at harvest — you'll never pay for an orange in this town again.
arc.grandline.marmalade_siege.after.town: Rotgut's gone and the still-house is cold. You can smell the blossom again.
Best festival in living memory! Shame about the east orchard. Worth it? Ask me next year.
They say you pulled every fuse yourself. The shops are giving the hero of the orchard a discount — that's you!
arc.grandline.clockwork_regatta.why: Gizmo Gearhart, the Tinker Pirate, stole the champion racing sloop of Syrup Village's old helmsman and seeded the regatta course with clockwork sharks. The children's race is the day after tomorrow.
arc.grandline.clockwork_regatta.cast.tom: 'Steady Hand', once the best helmsman in the East Blue — until he put a ship on the rocks under Reverse Mountain. He mends nets now and won't touch a tiller.
arc.grandline.clockwork_regatta.cast.giz: the Tinker Pirate. Builds wonderful things and points them at people.
arc.grandline.decision.syrup_helm: who takes the helm (talk to Tomas)
arc.grandline.site.syrup_dock: Syrup Village's dock, where Gizmo's crew winds the sharks
arc.grandline.site.syrup_keys: the key-room at the back of Gizmo's workshop
quest.grandline.syrup_sharks.desc: Gizmo's crew is winding clockwork sharks at Syrup Village's dock. Break 4 of them.
quest.grandline.syrup_workshop.desc: The winding keys come from Gizmo's workshop. Break 3 of his crew there and find out what he's really planning.
quest.grandline.syrup_choice.desc: Gizmo means to sink every boat in the regatta but his own — the children's too. Talk to Tomas and decide how to stop him.
quest.grandline.syrup_race.desc: Get Tomas aboard his old sloop: talk to him at the dock.
quest.grandline.syrup_keys.desc: Jam the sharks' winding keys: beat 3 of Gizmo's crew in his key-room.
scene.grandline.syrup_1.end.1: narrator|Syrup Village sits high on its plateau, and every child in it seems to own a boat. Today none of them are on the water.
scene.grandline.syrup_1.end.2: tomas|Don't look at the harbour. There's nothing on the harbour. That's the problem.
scene.grandline.syrup_1.end.3: tomas|Tomas Kajitori. I mend nets. I used to be a helmsman — best in the East Blue, they said, until I put a ship on the rocks at the foot of Reverse Mountain. I don't steer any more.
scene.grandline.syrup_1.end.4: tomas|A pirate called Gizmo stole my old racing sloop, the Kingfisher, and filled the regatta course with clockwork sharks. Wind-up teeth. The children's race is in two days.
scene.grandline.syrup_1.end.5: tomas|I can't stop him. I'm not sure I can stop anything. But you look like you might.
scene.grandline.syrup_sharks.end.1: narrator|One of Gizmo's crew drops a brass winding key as long as your arm. Stamped on the bow: PROPERTY OF G. GEARHART — WORKSHOP No. 2.
scene.grandline.syrup_sharks.end.2: tomas|They wind the sharks at his workshop. Every shark needs a key. No key, no teeth.
scene.grandline.syrup_workshop.end.1: narrator|Gizmo's workshop is a cathedral of gears. On the wall, a chalk map of the regatta course: every shark marked with a little red X, and a big one where the children's dinghies start.
scene.grandline.syrup_workshop.end.2: tomas|He's not racing. He's clearing the course. Every boat that isn't the Kingfisher goes to the bottom, and he wins by default.
scene.grandline.syrup_workshop.end.3: yuzu|Mister Tomas? Is the race still on? I painted my boat. It's got a duck on it.
scene.grandline.syrup_workshop.end.4: tomas|...Yes, Yuzu. The race is on.
scene.grandline.syrup_choice.talk.1: tomas|I said that. Why did I say that?
scene.grandline.syrup_choice.talk.2: you|Because it's true. The question is how.
scene.grandline.syrup_choice.talk.3: tomas|One way: somebody takes the Kingfisher back and races her through the course, drawing the sharks off the little ones while you deal with Gizmo. Somebody who can steer through teeth.
scene.grandline.syrup_choice.talk.4: tomas|...That would have to be me. My hands still shake on a tiller.
scene.grandline.syrup_choice.talk.5: tomas|The other way: we jam the winding keys before the race. Nobody sails until the water's safe. Gizmo's crew will be waiting in the key-room for us — but nobody small gets hurt.
scene.grandline.choice.syrup_helm.helm: Take the helm, Tomas. You're the only one who can, and the children are watching.
scene.grandline.choice.syrup_helm.keys: Jam the keys first. Nobody races until the water's safe.
scene.grandline.syrup_choice.end.helm.1: tomas|...All right. All right! Hold my nets. No — throw them away. I'm going to need both hands.
scene.grandline.syrup_choice.end.keys.1: tomas|Sensible. That's the word. Sensible. The key-room's at the back of the workshop. Mind the shark on the stairs — it's a decoy, but it bites.
scene.grandline.syrup_race.start.1: tomas|Find me at the dock when you're ready. If I'm not there, I've lost my nerve. Drag me.
scene.grandline.syrup_race.end.1: narrator|Tomas steps aboard the Kingfisher like a man stepping into a cold bath. Then his hands find the tiller, and something in his shoulders comes untied.
scene.grandline.syrup_race.end.3: tomas|Go. Keep Gizmo busy. I'll keep his sharks busy.
scene.grandline.syrup_keys.end.1: narrator|The last key comes out of its lock with a sad little twang. All over the bay, clockwork sharks go limp and bob to the surface, belly up.
scene.grandline.syrup_2.start.1: gizmo|Tick tock, tick tock! The regatta is MINE.
scene.grandline.syrup_2.start.helm.1: gizmo|My sharks! Why are my sharks chasing a SLOOP? Who's steering that — is that KAJITORI?
scene.grandline.syrup_2.start.helm.2: tomas|Afternoon, Gizmo. I'm told you've been sailing my boat badly.
scene.grandline.syrup_2.start.keys.1: gizmo|My keys! You unwound my beautiful sharks! Do you know how long it takes to wind a shark?
scene.grandline.syrup_2.end.1: narrator|Gizmo goes down in a shower of springs. The regatta is saved.
scene.grandline.syrup_2.end.helm.1: narrator|Gizmo goes down in a shower of springs. Out on the bay, the Kingfisher cuts through the last of the sharks and crosses the finish line with nobody racing her.
scene.grandline.syrup_2.end.helm.2: tomas|I steered. I actually steered. Somebody write that down.
scene.grandline.syrup_2.end.keys.1: narrator|Gizmo goes down in a shower of springs. The next morning, forty children's boats cross the bay without a single tooth in the water.
scene.grandline.syrup_2.end.keys.2: yuzu|I came FOURTH! The duck came fourth!
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.start.1: narrator|Tomas is down at the dock beside the Kingfisher, running a hand along her rail like an old friend's shoulder.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.1: tomas|You'll need a helmsman for the Grand Line. Ask me.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.2: tomas|The Baratie's under siege, they say. The floating restaurant.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.helm.1: tomas|I thought I'd never hold a tiller again. Turns out I just needed someone stubborn enough to put one in my hand.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.helm.2: tomas|There's a wreck at the foot of Reverse Mountain with my name on it. One day I want to sail past it and keep going.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.helm.3: tomas|You'll need a helmsman for the Grand Line. Steady hands. Mine are steady now. Ask me.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.helm.4: tomas|And if you're heading on — the Baratie's under siege. The floating restaurant. Some glutton's fleet wants the kitchen's recipe book.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.keys.1: tomas|Forty boats, and every child came home. That's a better finish than any race I ever won.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.keys.2: tomas|I still don't know if I can steer through a storm. But I'd like to find out with somebody who thinks before they sail.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.keys.3: tomas|You'll need a helmsman for the Grand Line. Ask me — before I lose my nerve again.
scene.grandline.recruit_tomas.end.keys.4: tomas|And if you're heading on — the Baratie's under siege. The floating restaurant. Some glutton's fleet wants the kitchen's recipe book.
recap.grandline.syrup_1: Reached Syrup Village, where the old helmsman Tomas told you about the stolen Kingfisher and the clockwork sharks.
recap.grandline.syrup_sharks: Broke Gizmo's shark-winders at the dock and found a key from his workshop.
recap.grandline.syrup_workshop: Raided Gizmo's workshop and found his real plan: clear the course by sinking every boat but his — the children's too.
recap.grandline.syrup_choice.helm: Talked Tomas into taking the helm again.
recap.grandline.syrup_choice.keys: Decided to jam the sharks' keys before anyone sailed.
recap.grandline.syrup_race: Tomas took the Kingfisher's tiller for the first time in years.
recap.grandline.syrup_keys: Pulled every winding key; the sharks floated belly up.
recap.grandline.syrup_2: Brought down Gizmo the Tinker Pirate.
recap.grandline.syrup_2.helm: Brought down Gizmo while Tomas steered the Kingfisher through his sharks.
recap.grandline.syrup_2.keys: Brought down Gizmo; forty children raced a safe bay the next morning.
recap.grandline.recruit_tomas: Tomas found his nerve. He'll take your helm if you ask — and the Baratie is under siege.
arc.grandline.clockwork_regatta.bonus.he: Tomas presses his old Log Pose into your hand. 'I won't need it on dry land, and I'm not staying on dry land.'
arc.grandline.clockwork_regatta.bonus.ke: The village took up a collection: 1,500 Beli, and Syrup Village's shops give you 15% off from now on.
arc.grandline.clockwork_regatta.aid.helm: The Kingfisher cuts across the bay behind you, scattering Gizmo's crew. You find your footing faster for it.
arc.grandline.recruit_hint.tomas: Tomas will join your crew if you ask: talk to him and invite him aboard.
arc.grandline.clockwork_regatta.after.to: The Kingfisher's in the water and so am I, near enough.
My hands haven't shaken since the race. Don't tell anyone; they'll want me to mend their nets again.
Forty boats, forty children home. I count them every time I close my eyes. It's a nice thing to count.
No sharks in the bay! You can hear the kids from the plateau.
Old Kajitori steered through a pack of sharks! Can you believe it? He's been insufferable since.
Every child home safe. The village took up a collection for you — and the shops will knock something off. Don't argue.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.why: The Gourmand's glutton fleet has the floating restaurant surrounded and demands the kitchen's recipe book. Its last page is the old owner's chart of every supply route in the East Blue — the sloops that feed the islands.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.cast.ken: 'the Carving Knife', the Baratie's head waiter. Two carving blades, impeccable manners, and no patience at all for people who don't say please.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.cast.hor: 'Hambone', a Marine vice admiral on a very long lunch break. Insists he is off duty.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.cast.fos: 'the Gourmand', captain of the glutton fleet. Has eaten forty-one restaurants and is still hungry.
arc.grandline.decision.baratie_plan: how to answer the Gourmand (talk to Kenji)
quest.grandline.baratie_boarders.desc: Fosco's men are eating the Baratie bare without paying. Throw 5 of them off the dining deck.
quest.grandline.baratie_book.desc: Vice Admiral Horatio has been at table one for six days and knows why Fosco wants the recipe book. Talk to him.
quest.grandline.baratie_choice.desc: The Gourmand's flagship is coming about. Kenji and Horatio each have a plan. Talk to Kenji and decide how to answer him.
quest.grandline.baratie_feast.desc: Take Kenji's forged recipe book to Fosco 'the Gourmand' — personally, with a bow.
quest.grandline.baratie_guard.desc: Horatio's squadron is on its way. Until then, beat 3 of Fosco's bodyguards on the Baratie's deck.
scene.grandline.baratie_1.end.1: narrator|The Baratie rides at anchor like a fat wooden duck, ringed by ships flying a crossed knife and fork. Inside, every table is full of pirates who have not paid.
scene.grandline.baratie_1.end.2: kenji|Welcome to the Baratie. Table for one? Please wipe your boots. The gentlemen at tables four through nineteen are not leaving, and they are not tipping.
scene.grandline.baratie_1.end.3: kenji|Kenji Escoffier, head waiter. I would normally serve them to the sea in two neat portions, but the head chef has asked me not to start a war during service.
scene.grandline.baratie_1.end.4: kenji|You, however, are a customer. Customers may do as they please. Please.
scene.grandline.baratie_boarders.end.1: narrator|The last boarder goes over the rail. Pinned to the menu board with a steak knife: a letter on greasy paper.
scene.grandline.baratie_boarders.end.2: kenji|'Deliver the recipe book by sundown or I eat the restaurant. Sincerely, F. Ragout.' He has signed it with a gravy stain.
scene.grandline.baratie_boarders.end.3: kenji|The Vice Admiral at table one may know something. He has been at table one for six days.
scene.grandline.baratie_book.end.1: horatio|Mmf — I'm off duty. Off duty means I'm eating. ...Oh, the recipe book? Yes, I know why he wants it.
scene.grandline.baratie_book.end.2: horatio|The old owner was a smuggler before he was a cook. The last page of that book is his chart of every supply route in the East Blue — every sloop that feeds every island.
scene.grandline.baratie_book.end.3: horatio|With that chart, the Gourmand raids the supply lines and the whole Blue goes hungry. Then he sells the food back. Clever pig.
scene.grandline.baratie_book.end.4: kenji|His flagship is coming about. He's done waiting for sundown.
scene.grandline.baratie_choice.talk.1: kenji|I have a proposal. I write him a recipe book — a beautiful one, with gold edges — full of the worst recipes ever devised. Eel jam. Boiled boots. Custard of regret.
scene.grandline.baratie_choice.talk.2: kenji|His crew will cook the feast he orders from it, and his crew will spend the evening in the hold. I will stand beside you when the Gourmand comes for his dessert.
scene.grandline.baratie_choice.talk.3: horatio|Or — and I say this purely as a diner — I have a squadron two hours south. Technically on exercise. I call them in, they take the fleet. His bodyguards will still be aboard, mind.
scene.grandline.baratie_choice.talk.4: horatio|But the book comes with me. Evidence. The Marines keep that chart where no pirate can get it — including your restaurant, young man.
scene.grandline.baratie_choice.talk.5: kenji|The Baratie has kept that book for forty years, Vice Admiral.
scene.grandline.baratie_choice.talk.6: horatio|And I have kept my lunch for six days. We all make sacrifices.
scene.grandline.choice.baratie_plan.forg: Serve Fosco a forged book. Let his crew eat the custard of regret.
scene.grandline.choice.baratie_plan.squa: Call in Horatio's squadron. The chart goes to the Marines, where no pirate can use it.
scene.grandline.baratie_choice.end.forge: kenji|Excellent. Give me an hour and a quill. Then take it to the Gourmand — personally, with a bow. He likes a bow.
scene.grandline.baratie_choice.end.squad: horatio|Mmf. Fine. Somebody pass me the Den Den Mushi. And the bread rolls.
scene.grandline.baratie_feast.end.1: fosco|THE BOOK! Finally! 'Eel Jam with a Coulis of Despair'... magnificent! Cook EVERYTHING!
scene.grandline.baratie_feast.end.2: narrator|An hour later the glutton fleet's galley crews are groaning in their holds. Only the Gourmand, who eats last, is still on his feet — and he has reached the dessert page.
scene.grandline.baratie_feast.end.3: fosco|'Custard of Regret'... THIS IS A FORGERY!
scene.grandline.baratie_guard.start.1: horatio|The squadron's on its way. Until then, his bodyguards are on our deck, and they look hungry.
scene.grandline.baratie_guard.end.1: narrator|On the horizon, Marine sails close around the glutton fleet like a lid on a pot. On the deck, the Gourmand stands alone and very, very hungry.
scene.grandline.baratie_2.start.1: fosco|BRING ME THE RECIPE BOOK! I am still HUNGRY!
fosco|I DON'T PAY BILLS. I EAT THEM.
scene.grandline.baratie_2.start.squadron: fosco|My fleet! You called the MARINES? On a RESTAURANT?
scene.grandline.baratie_2.end.1: narrator|The Gourmand goes down like a collapsing soufflé. The Baratie is open for business.
scene.grandline.baratie_2.end.forgery.1: narrator|The Gourmand goes down like a collapsing soufflé. Kenji wipes both blades on a napkin and folds it into a swan.
scene.grandline.baratie_2.end.forgery.2: kenji|The book stays in the kitchen, where it belongs. The head chef would like you to know you may eat here for free. Within reason. He said 'within reason' twice.
scene.grandline.baratie_2.end.squadron.1: narrator|The Gourmand goes down like a collapsing soufflé. The Marine squadron tows his fleet away in a long, sulky line.
scene.grandline.baratie_2.end.squadron.2: horatio|The chart's in Marine hands now. No pirate raids those supply lines on my watch. Here — for your trouble. And I paid your bill. And mine. Mostly mine.
scene.grandline.recruit_kenji.start.1: narrator|Kenji is laying the tables for dinner service, folding every napkin into a perfect swan.
scene.grandline.recruit_kenji.end.1: kenji|If you need a swordsman, Captain, please ask.
scene.grandline.recruit_kenji.end.2: kenji|A Fish-Man pirate has walled up Cocoyasi's waterfront. You may want to visit.
scene.grandline.recruit_kenji.end.forger: kenji|I stood beside you against the Gourmand, and I found I liked it. Not the violence. The standing beside.
kenji|There is a swordsman at the end of the world — Jinpachi, the Last Blade. I would like to learn from him a cut that serves, rather than one that merely cuts. I cannot do that from table one.
kenji|If you need a swordsman, Captain, please ask. I will say yes. Thank you.
kenji|One more thing. A Fish-Man pirate has walled up the waterfront at Cocoyasi and taxes the tangerines. A regular of ours. He never tips.
scene.grandline.recruit_kenji.end.squadr: kenji|The book is gone, but the kitchen is still here, and so are the people in it. I suppose that is the right way round.
kenji|There is a swordsman at the end of the world — Jinpachi, the Last Blade. I would like to learn from him a cut that serves, rather than one that merely cuts.
kenji|If you need a swordsman, Captain, please ask. I will say yes. Thank you.
kenji|One more thing. A Fish-Man pirate has walled up the waterfront at Cocoyasi and taxes the tangerines. A regular of ours. He never tips.
recap.grandline.baratie_1: Reached the Baratie, besieged by the Gourmand's glutton fleet, and met Kenji the head waiter.
recap.grandline.baratie_boarders: Threw the non-paying boarders over the rail and found Fosco's ultimatum.
recap.grandline.baratie_book: Learned from Vice Admiral Horatio why Fosco wants the book: its last page charts every supply route in the East Blue.
recap.grandline.baratie_choice.forgery: Decided to serve Fosco a forged recipe book.
recap.grandline.baratie_choice.squadron: Decided to let Horatio's squadron take the glutton fleet.
recap.grandline.baratie_feast: Delivered the forged book; the glutton fleet spent the evening in its holds.
recap.grandline.baratie_guard: Held the deck against Fosco's bodyguards while the Marine squadron closed in.
recap.grandline.baratie_2.forgery: Brought down the Gourmand with Kenji at your side. The book stays in the Baratie's kitchen.
recap.grandline.baratie_2.squadron: Brought down the Gourmand; the Marines took his fleet and the supply chart.
recap.grandline.recruit_kenji: Kenji wants to learn from the Last Blade. He'll join if you ask — and Cocoyasi has trouble with a Fish-Man pirate.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.bonus.fo: The head chef sends you off with two plates of Saltfire Curry, and the Baratie's cooks will sell you the house specials from now on.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.bonus.sq: Horatio pays your bill, his bill, and 2,500 Beli 'for services to lunch'. The Marines remember who helped.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.aid.forg: Kenji falls in beside you, a carving blade in each hand. 'After you. Please.' Your blows land harder with him covering your flank.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.aid.squa: Marine sails close in on the horizon and Fosco's men keep glancing at them. They hit you less often, and less hard.
arc.grandline.recruit_hint.kenji: Kenji will join your crew if you ask: talk to him and invite him aboard.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.after.ke: Table for one? For you, always. Please.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.after.ho: Mmf. Still off duty. Have you tried the dessert? Don't try the custard.
That forged book is the funniest thing I've read in thirty years of service. I've ordered a copy.
My squadron's been insufferable since we bagged the Gourmand. Good work, civilian. Sit, sit — the bread rolls are on me.
arc.grandline.feast_under_siege.after.to: The glutton fleet's gone! Order anything. Except the custard.
Chef says you eat free. Within reason. He said 'within reason' twice. And we're selling the house specials again — ask at the counter.
The Marines took the whole glutton fleet! And the old book. Chef's still sulking about the book.
arc.grandline.coral_keep.why: Gorgo 'Hammerjaw' walled Cocoyasi's waterfront into a fortress and taxes every tangerine on the island. When the harvest came up short, he took the village children as 'collateral'.
arc.grandline.coral_keep.cast.kaimon: 'Seawall', a Fish-Man karate master who followed Gorgo for Fish-Man pride and left when pride started meaning children in cellars.
arc.grandline.coral_keep.cast.gorgo: 'Hammerjaw', Fish-Man pirate and lord of the Coral Keep. Believes humans owe him, and collects.
arc.grandline.decision.coco_plan: how Cocoyasi fights back (talk to Kaimon)
arc.grandline.site.coco_cellar: the cellars under the Coral Keep
quest.grandline.coco_grove.desc: The villagers won't speak to Kaimon. Talk to 2 of them for him and find out what Gorgo did when the harvest came up short.
quest.grandline.coco_cellar.desc: Gorgo holds eight children in the cellars under the Coral Keep. Beat 3 of his guards there and bring them out.
quest.grandline.coco_choice.desc: Gorgo means to break the seawall tonight and let the tide into the village. Talk to Kaimon and decide how Cocoyasi fights back.
quest.grandline.coco_gate.desc: Stand at the Coral Keep's gate beside Kaimon and break 2 of Gorgo's brutes.
quest.grandline.coco_seawall.desc: Get the village out to hold its own seawall: talk to 3 villagers.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_1.end.1: narrator|Cocoyasi's waterfront has vanished behind a wall of grey coral, studded with shells and bad intentions. Above the gate, a sign: TANGERINE TAX — PAY HERE — OR ELSE.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_1.end.2: kaimon|Stand aside, human — or stand with me. Those two were Gorgo's gate guards. I used to drink with them.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_1.end.3: kaimon|Kaimon Funaboshi. I followed Hammerjaw because he promised Fish-Men pride. Taxing children's tangerines is not pride. I left this morning. Loudly.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_1.end.4: kaimon|The villagers won't speak to me. I don't blame them. But they'll speak to you.
scene.grandline.coco_grove.end.1: resident|...He's with you? The shark? Fine. Fine. Listen — the harvest came up short this year, and Gorgo didn't like the count.
scene.grandline.coco_grove.end.2: resident|He took the children. Eight of them. 'Collateral', he said, until we pay double. They're in the cellars under the Keep.
scene.grandline.coco_grove.end.3: kaimon|...I didn't know. I swear on the sea, I didn't know. I'm going in now. With or without you.
scene.grandline.coco_cellar.end.1: narrator|The cellar door gives. Eight small faces blink in the light. The smallest looks up at Kaimon and does not run.
scene.grandline.coco_cellar.end.2: kanta|You're the one who left. Mum says you shouted at Hammerjaw. Did you really shout at Hammerjaw?
scene.grandline.coco_cellar.end.4: narrator|From the top of the Keep, a conch horn sounds. Gorgo knows. Tonight he means to break the seawall and let the tide into the village.
scene.grandline.coco_choice.talk.1: kaimon|He'll come through the Keep's gate with his brutes and the tide behind him. Someone has to hold that gate.
scene.grandline.coco_choice.talk.2: kaimon|If we stand there together — a human and a Fish-Man — the village sees it. Maybe they stop looking at me like a shark. Maybe they stop looking at all of us like that.
scene.grandline.coco_choice.talk.3: resident|Or we hold our own seawall. We've got shovels, boats and forty years of grudges. Let the Fish-Man guard the children — we'll guard the island.
scene.grandline.coco_choice.talk.4: kaimon|If the village holds the wall, Gorgo comes straight for you and me without his brutes. If I stand at the gate, they'll see me fight — but they won't see themselves win.
scene.grandline.choice.coco_plan.side_by: Fight beside Kaimon at the Keep's gate. Let the village see a Fish-Man stand for them.
scene.grandline.choice.coco_plan.seawall: Rally the villagers to hold the seawall themselves. It's their island.
scene.grandline.coco_choice.end.side_by_: kaimon|Then we hold the gate. Brutes first. Keep your feet planted — Fish-Man karate hits like a wave, and waves don't care who's standing in them.
resident|Right! Everyone with a shovel, to the seawall! Kaimon — mind the little ones. ...Please.
scene.grandline.coco_gate.end.1: narrator|The second brute drops into the surf. Gorgo's roar shakes the Keep, and the gate swings open from the inside.
scene.grandline.coco_seawall.start.1: resident|We need every hand on the seawall. Go round the village and get them out here — the stubborn ones too.
scene.grandline.coco_seawall.end.1: narrator|Forty villagers line the seawall with shovels, oars and one very angry goat. When the tide comes, it breaks against them and goes no further.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_2.start.1: gorgo|Humans pay the tangerine tax or they pay in teeth. Grrahaha!
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_2.start.side_by: gorgo|KAIMON. You'd stand with these PEELERS?
kaimon|I'd stand with anyone you're standing on.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_2.start.seawall: gorgo|Fine. I'll take it out of you.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_2.end.1: narrator|Hammerjaw goes down in the gateway of his own Keep. Cocoyasi's tangerines belong to Cocoyasi again.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_2.end.side_by_s: narrator|Hammerjaw goes down in the gateway of his own Keep. Kaimon catches the falling sign — TANGERINE TAX — and snaps it over his knee.
resident|...Thank you. Both of you. Kaimon, you'll — you'll stay for dinner? The children want you to stay for dinner.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_2.end.seawall.1: narrator|Hammerjaw goes down in the gateway of his own Keep. Behind you, the village cheers itself hoarse from the seawall.
scene.grandline.cocoyasi_2.end.seawall.2: kaimon|They did it. They held it themselves. ...They're still not looking at me. That's all right. It was their fight.
scene.grandline.recruit_kaimon.start.1: narrator|Kaimon is on the beach outside the broken Keep, teaching three children how to stand like a wave.
scene.grandline.recruit_kaimon.end.1: kaimon|If your crew needs a fighter who hits like the sea, ask me.
scene.grandline.recruit_kaimon.end.2: kaimon|Loguetown's north-west. Every rookie ends up there sooner or later.
scene.grandline.recruit_kaimon.end.side_: kaimon|They let me eat at their table. A Fish-Man, at a human table, passing the tangerines. That's the beginning of something.
kaimon|I want to see more beginnings. At Sabaody they sell people like me at auction. One day I'd like to walk in there with a human friend and close it down.
kaimon|If your crew needs a fighter who hits like the sea, ask me.
kaimon|And if you're sailing north-west: Loguetown. Where the Saltfire King died. Every rookie ends up there sooner or later.
scene.grandline.recruit_kaimon.end.seawa: kaimon|They held their own wall. Good. I've learned something: you can't be forgiven by people you've frightened. You can only be useful until they forget to be frightened.
kaimon|At Sabaody they sell people like me at auction. One day I'd like to walk in there with a human friend and close it down.
kaimon|If your crew needs a fighter who hits like the sea, ask me.
kaimon|And if you're sailing north-west: Loguetown. Where the Saltfire King died. Every rookie ends up there sooner or later.
recap.grandline.cocoyasi_1: Broke through the Coral Keep's gate guards and met Kaimon, who had left Gorgo's crew that morning.
recap.grandline.coco_grove: The villagers told you the truth: Gorgo took eight children as 'collateral' for the tangerine tax.
recap.grandline.coco_cellar: Opened the Keep's cellars and brought the children out — and Gorgo sounded his horn.
recap.grandline.coco_choice.side_by_side: Decided to hold the Keep's gate beside Kaimon.
recap.grandline.coco_choice.seawall: Decided the village would hold its own seawall.
recap.grandline.coco_gate: Held the gate with Kaimon against Gorgo's brutes.
recap.grandline.coco_seawall: Rallied the village; forty people and a goat held the seawall against the tide.
recap.grandline.cocoyasi_2.side_by_side: Brought Hammerjaw down at his own gate with Kaimon beside you. The village asked Kaimon to stay for dinner.
recap.grandline.cocoyasi_2.seawall: Brought Hammerjaw down while the village held its own seawall.
recap.grandline.recruit_kaimon: Kaimon wants to see Fish-Men and humans side by side. He'll join if you ask — and Loguetown waits to the north-west.
arc.grandline.coral_keep.bonus.side_by_s: Kaimon shows you a stance he learned long before he ever met Gorgo, and writes it down for you: a Fish-Man Karate scroll.
arc.grandline.coral_keep.bonus.seawall: The village pools its tangerine money: 2,000 Beli, and Cocoyasi's shops give you the islander's price (15% off) from now on.
arc.grandline.coral_keep.aid.side_by_sid: Kaimon plants himself beside you in the gateway. Blows meant for you break on him like waves on a seawall.
arc.grandline.recruit_hint.kaimon: Kaimon will join your crew if you ask: talk to him and invite him aboard.
arc.grandline.coral_keep.after.kaimon: The children are learning karate. The adults are learning to say hello. Both are slow. Both are coming along.
arc.grandline.coral_keep.after.townsfolk: The Keep's empty and the tangerines are ours again. Take one. Take two.
You and the Fish-Man held the gate! Kaimon comes to dinner on Sundays now. He brings fish. It's very awkward and very nice.
We held the seawall ourselves! Forty of us and Mrs. Hoshi's goat. The shops give you the islander's price, you hear?
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings: The Town of Beginnings and Endings
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.why: Every road in the East Blue ends at the platform where the Saltfire King died. It's the anniversary: rookies pour in, Captain Valka means to close the harbour on all of them, and a forecaster's stolen almanac says a storm will break at midnight.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.cast.od: 'the Weathervane', forecaster and chart-forger, saving up for the first almanac of the Grand Line's impossible weather.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.cast.ba: 'Inkwell', East Blue chief of the Sea-Gull Gazette. Everything is a scoop if you print it big enough.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.cast.va: 'the White Squall', the Marine captain who has caught every rookie this year.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.cast.to: 'Firecracker', a rival rookie with the Bomb-Bomb Fruit and no indoor voice.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.cast.pi: 'Rainmaker', a Revolutionary agent with an umbrella and opinions about storms.
arc.grandline.decision.logue_plan: where you'll be at midnight (talk to Odile)
arc.grandline.site.logue_alleys: the alleys behind Odile's chart shop
arc.grandline.site.logue_platform_watch: the Marine watch around the execution platform
quest.grandline.logue_odile.desc: Bartolo's 'crackpot' forecaster keeps a chart shop on Harbour Street. Talk to Odile Kazamidori.
quest.grandline.logue_pages.desc: Bandits stole Odile's almanac pages. Beat 5 of them in the alleys behind her shop and bring the pages back.
quest.grandline.logue_choice.desc: A storm breaks at midnight, the Saltfire rises at the same hour, and Valka is closing the harbour. Talk to Odile and decide where you'll be.
quest.grandline.logue_platform.desc: Find Bartolo. If you're going to stand on the execution platform at midnight, you'll want a photographer.
quest.grandline.logue_shelter.desc: Get Harbour Street ready for the storm: talk to 3 townsfolk and get the stalls under cover.
scene.grandline.logue_1.end.1: narrator|Loguetown: a city of stone, salt and souvenirs. In the main square stands the execution platform, black against the sky. Everybody looks at it. Nobody says so.
scene.grandline.logue_1.end.2: bartolo|Scoop! Scoop! You've got the face of a front page! Bartolo, Sea-Gull Gazette, East Blue bureau. Anniversary week — the whole Blue's in town.
scene.grandline.logue_1.end.3: bartolo|Every rookie with a dream, Captain Valka with a net, and a forecaster on Harbour Street who swears blind there's a storm coming at midnight. On a clear night! That's a scoop or a crackpot. Go and find out which.
scene.grandline.logue_odile.end.1: odile|Charts! Genuine Grand Line charts, only slightly invented! ...Oh, you're not buying. You're LOOKING. Nobody looks.
scene.grandline.logue_odile.end.2: odile|Odile Kazamidori. I forge charts to pay for my life's work: the first almanac that can predict the Grand Line's weather. Everyone laughs. Then it rains.
scene.grandline.logue_odile.end.3: odile|And now it's gone. Bandits broke in last night and took the almanac pages — forty years of tide tables, my grandmother's and mine. They think it's a treasure map.
scene.grandline.logue_odile.end.4: odile|It IS a treasure map, technically. The treasure is knowing when it's going to rain.
scene.grandline.logue_pages.end.1: narrator|The almanac pages come back crumpled but whole. Odile smooths them out on a barrel and goes very quiet.
scene.grandline.logue_pages.end.2: odile|Midnight. The storm breaks at midnight — and look here: the same night every year, the same hour, the pale flame on the horizon. The Saltfire. My grandmother saw it from this street.
scene.grandline.logue_pages.end.3: odile|And Valka knows about the storm. She's closing the harbour at eleven. Every rookie in the city trapped between the platform and the sea, with the storm on top of them.
scene.grandline.logue_pages.end.4: tobias|HEY! YOU! Are you a rookie too? MIDNIGHT! THE PLATFORM! LOSER BUYS MEAT!
scene.grandline.logue_pages.end.5: odile|...And that one's going to get himself arrested in a lightning storm.
scene.grandline.logue_choice.talk.1: odile|Here's the thing about the platform. At midnight, when the Saltfire shows, every eye in Loguetown will be on it. The Gazette, the Marines, the rookies — everyone.
scene.grandline.logue_choice.talk.2: odile|Stand up there and the whole East Blue knows your face by breakfast. Valka will never stop chasing you. Some people want that.
scene.grandline.logue_choice.talk.3: odile|Or: the storm. The market stalls on Harbour Street will go into the sea, and half the town lives off them. Get them under cover first and you'll miss the flame — but nobody drowns.
scene.grandline.logue_choice.talk.4: bartolo|Either way, I'm printing it. 'ROOKIE STANDS ON THE PLATFORM' or 'ROOKIE SAVES MARKET'. Both sell. The first one sells MORE.
scene.grandline.choice.logue_plan.platfo: Stand on the execution platform at midnight. Let the whole East Blue see you.
scene.grandline.choice.logue_plan.shelte: Get Harbour Street under cover before the storm. Nobody drowns.
scene.grandline.logue_choice.end.platfor: odile|Then go and find Bartolo. If you're going to do something reckless, you may as well have a photographer.
scene.grandline.logue_choice.end.shelter: odile|Good. Start with the stalls by the fish market — they never listen to me, but they might listen to you.
scene.grandline.logue_platform.end.1: narrator|At a quarter to midnight you climb the platform's steps. Below, the square is packed. The wind turns; the first drops fall.
scene.grandline.logue_platform.end.2: bartolo|Hold still! HOLD STILL! That's the one. That's the photo of the decade!
scene.grandline.logue_platform.end.3: narrator|And there, out on the black sea beyond the harbour wall: a pale blue flame, dancing on the water. The whole square gasps. Captain Valka's head turns from the flame — to you.
scene.grandline.logue_shelter.end.1: narrator|By midnight the stalls are lashed down, the fishwives are in the chapel, and the last cart rolls in under the arches as the storm hits like a wall.
scene.grandline.logue_shelter.end.2: narrator|You miss the flame. You hear it, though — the gasp that goes through the whole city at once — and Odile, beside you, saying very quietly: 'There it is.'
scene.grandline.logue_2.start.1: narrator|Lightning splits the sky over Loguetown. Rookies, Marines and one very loud firecracker, all in the same square.
scene.grandline.logue_2.start.platform.1: tobias|YOU! On the PLATFORM! That was MY idea! Come down here and FIGHT ME!
scene.grandline.logue_2.start.platform.2: narrator|Lightning splits the sky. Valka's Marines pour into the square.
scene.grandline.logue_2.start.shelter.1: tobias|There you are! I stood on the platform ALL BY MYSELF and nobody even LOOKED! I'm SO ANGRY!
scene.grandline.logue_2.start.shelter.2: narrator|Lightning splits the sky. Valka's Marines are closing the square — Tobias is in the middle of it, and so are you.
scene.grandline.logue_2.end.1: narrator|The storm blows itself out by dawn. Loguetown wakes up tired, wet, and talking about the flame.
scene.grandline.logue_2.end.platform.1: valka|Next time, rookie. There's always a next time. I'll be there for it.
scene.grandline.logue_2.end.platform.2: bartolo|FRONT PAGE! Tomorrow morning, every port in the East Blue! You're famous! Or wanted! Same thing, really!
scene.grandline.logue_2.end.shelter.1: valka|You were on Harbour Street when the storm hit, moving stalls. ...That wasn't nothing. Don't let it go to your head.
scene.grandline.logue_2.end.shelter.2: bartolo|'ROOKIE SAVES MARKET.' Page four. It'll sell. Not as well. But it'll sell.
scene.grandline.recruit_odile.start.1: narrator|Odile has spread her almanac across three tables of the harbour inn and is adding a fresh page in a shaking hand: THE SALTFIRE — SEEN AGAIN.
scene.grandline.recruit_odile.end.1: odile|I'm a navigator, and I want to chart the Grand Line. Ask me.
scene.grandline.recruit_odile.end.2: odile|The flame points to the Twin Capes, at the foot of Reverse Mountain.
scene.grandline.recruit_odile.end.platfo: odile|I watched you up there with the flame behind you. I've been charting that light my whole life and I've never been closer than this street.
odile|I want to finish the almanac. That means the Grand Line — the real weather, the impossible weather. That means a ship. That means you.
odile|I'm a navigator. The best navigator in the East Blue who's never left it. Ask me.
odile|And the flame's heading is in the almanac now: to the Twin Capes, at the foot of Reverse Mountain. Where the sea flows uphill.
scene.grandline.recruit_odile.end.shelte: odile|You gave up the flame to tie down fish stalls. I didn't think anyone did that. I've stopped being surprised by you; it's restful.
odile|I want to finish the almanac. That means the Grand Line — the real weather, the impossible weather. That means a ship. That means you.
odile|And the flame's heading is in the almanac now: to the Twin Capes, at the foot of Reverse Mountain. Where the sea flows uphill.
scene.grandline.logue_3.start.1: odile|Reverse Mountain. The sea goes up it. Don't ask me how; that's what the almanac is for.
recap.grandline.logue_1: Reached Loguetown on the Saltfire King's anniversary and met Bartolo of the Sea-Gull Gazette.
recap.grandline.logue_odile: Met Odile the Weathervane, whose almanac pages had been stolen.
recap.grandline.logue_pages: Took Odile's almanac back from the bandits: a storm at midnight, the Saltfire at the same hour, and Valka closing the harbour.
recap.grandline.logue_choice.platform: Decided to stand on the platform at midnight.
recap.grandline.logue_choice.shelter: Decided to get Harbour Street under cover before the storm.
recap.grandline.logue_platform: Stood on the execution platform as the Saltfire rose. Bartolo got his photo of the decade.
recap.grandline.logue_shelter: Lashed down Harbour Street before the storm hit. You missed the flame; nobody drowned.
recap.grandline.logue_2: Came through the storm, the rookies and Captain Valka's net.
recap.grandline.logue_2.platform: Came through the storm with your face on tomorrow's front page — and Captain Valka's attention for good.
recap.grandline.logue_2.shelter: Came through the storm; Captain Valka gave you a grudging nod.
recap.grandline.recruit_odile: Odile wants to chart the Grand Line. She'll navigate if you ask.
recap.grandline.logue_3: Followed the Saltfire's heading to the Twin Capes at the foot of Reverse Mountain.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.bonus.p: The Gazette prints your face on every front page in the East Blue; Bartolo sends you a framed copy. Pirates salute you, and Captain Valka has your photograph pinned above her desk.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.bonus.s: Harbour Street survived the storm. The market pays you 3,000 Beli, and Loguetown's shops give you 10% off from now on.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.aid.pla: The crowd around the platform is roaring for you. Every blow lands harder with the whole square watching.
arc.grandline.recruit_hint.odile: Odile will join your crew if you ask: talk to her and invite her aboard.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.after.o: The almanac's waiting for a ship. So am I. Hint, hint.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.after.v: Every rookie passes through Loguetown. Some of them are worth remembering. Don't make me regret saying so.
You. The one on the platform. Every Marine in the East Blue has your photograph now. I hope you like being looked at.
The rookie who moved fish stalls in a lightning storm. I'm still deciding whether that was brave or stupid. I suspect both.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.after.b: Scoop! What a week. What a WEEK.
My photo of the decade! Signed copies, half price. For you, full price — you're famous now.
'Rookie Saves Market' — page four, and the letters are still coming in. People LIKED it. I may have misjudged the market.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.after.t: What a night. The flame, the storm... Loguetown will talk about it for twenty years.
You're the one on the front page! On the platform! With the flame behind you! Can I touch your sleeve?
You're the one who tied down Harbour Street! My mother's stall survived because of you. The shops round here won't charge you full price.
arc.grandline.beginnings_endings.after.m: Captain Valka has your photograph pinned above her desk. That's not a compliment.
Captain Valka says you're to be watched, not chased. That's practically a medal.
